business: TradeCatch (a bilingual AI phone receptionist for Québec contractors)
target: Owner-operators of small trade businesses (1 to 10 people) in Montréal, Laval, Mirabel and Vaudreuil-Dorion who are on job sites all day, miss calls, and lose jobs to the next company on Google

segments.name: Solo plumber or electrician, one truck (business revenue)
Small plumbing/HVAC crew, 2 to 5 people (business revenue)
Renovation, roofing or landscaping contractor, seasonal (business revenue)
Established 6 to 10 person shop with an office person (business revenue)

behaviours.name: Lets it ring, calls back at lunch
behaviours.how: Calls go to voicemail while on site; calls back when there is a minute; knows some callers never pick up again.

behaviours.name: Spouse or partner handles the phone
behaviours.how: A spouse or family member answers when they can and keeps the details in a notebook or a text thread.

behaviours.name: Already on Jobber or Housecall Pro
behaviours.how: Runs quotes and invoices in Jobber; has seen its $29 receptionist add-on and the Google Calendar sync.

behaviours.name: Burned by a tool before
behaviours.how: Paid monthly for a CRM or lead service that nobody set up properly, cancelled after a fight, wary of anything recurring.

behaviours.name: Word-of-mouth only, no website
behaviours.how: Work comes from referrals and the Google Maps listing; distrusts anything that sounds like software or marketing.

behaviours.name: About to hire a human
behaviours.how: Considering a part-time office person at around $20 an hour; compares every tool to that cost and to what a person can do.

behaviours.name: French-first, tech-wary
behaviours.how: Works in French, texts rather than emails, will not sign anything long, and worries most about how it will sound to long-time clients.

objections: 2 000 $ before I've even heard it answer one of my calls?
Voxify is 300 $ a month with no setup fee.
What happens at 11 p.m. when it's an emergency and it can't transfer the call to me?
My Jobber already has a receptionist for 29 $.
My clients will hang up on a robot, especially in French.
Where do the recordings go? Is it in the States?
I've paid for software before that nobody set up properly.
My wife already answers the phone.
What if I hit the minute allowance in January?
habits: you are up a ladder or under a sink when the phone rings
you quote three jobs a week and chase maybe one
you check your phone at lunch and again at 6 p.m.
your Google listing has 23 reviews and you have replied to none
winter is your busy season and you lose track of callbacks
you do your invoicing on Sunday night
you speak French on the job and English with half your Laval customers
you lost a $9,000 kitchen job last month because the quote sat unanswered
